relations.subject: tool:couchbase-cli-setting-master-password
relations.evidence: This master password can be passed to the server using the couchbase-cli master-password command.

relations.subject: tool:couchbase-cli-setting-master-password
relations.evidence: Specifies the username of the user executing the command. If you do not have a user account with permission to execute the command then it will fail with an unauthorized error.

relations.subject: tool:couchbase-cli-setting-master-password
relations.evidence: This tool supports authenticating against a Couchbase Cluster by using certificate based authentication (mTLS authentication). To use certificate based authentication a certificate/key must be supplied, there a currently multiple ways this may be done.

relations.subject: tool:couchbase-cli-setting-master-password
relations.evidence: An encrypted PKCS#12 certificate/key may be provided using: - `--client-cert <path>`\- `--client-cert-password <password>`

notable_absence.finding: No role:/privilege: concept is cited; authorization is stated only generically ('If you do not have a user account with permission to execute the command then it will fail with an unauthorized error') without naming which role or privilege grants that permission - unlike user-manage.md's --delete/--list/--set options, which at least name 'full administrator privileges' explicitly. This page is vaguer still: it never says WHICH permission is required to set the master password, only that lacking permission fails.

cross_component_finding: The SYNOPSIS line lists a flag `[--rotate-password]` that does not exist anywhere in the OPTIONS section or EXAMPLES - the actual flag documented under OPTIONS is `--rotate-data-key` ('This option is used to generate a new data key file.'). This is a synopsis/options-section name mismatch: a reader following the SYNOPSIS literally would pass a flag the tool's own OPTIONS section never defines. This is precisely the kind of literal, unreviewed drift this round's authorship-provenance hypothesis predicts for engineer-authored, lightly-TW-reviewed CLI reference pages - the SYNOPSIS block and the OPTIONS prose look like they were edited independently and never reconciled.
